DClutter 1.1.0
==============

Thanks for trying this out.

DClutter shows you one file at a time from your Downloads folder and lets
you keep it, put it in the Trash, or file it into a folder — with one key
or one swipe. It opens on Downloads, and you can point it at any other
folder you like.


HOW TO OPEN IT (please read — the first launch will fail on purpose)
--------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Drag DClutter.app into your Applications folder.

2. Double-click it.

   macOS WILL REFUSE TO OPEN IT. This is expected. Keep going.

3. Open System Settings, go to Privacy & Security, and scroll all the way
   to the bottom. You'll see a line about DClutter being blocked, with an
   "Open Anyway" button. Click it.

4. Click "Open" to confirm.

That's the whole thing, and only on the first launch. Afterwards it opens
like any other app.


WHY DOES THAT HAPPEN?
---------------------

macOS blocks apps that haven't been signed with an Apple Developer
certificate, which costs $99 a year. This one hasn't been, yet. The
warning is macOS saying "I can't check who made this", not "this app is
broken or dangerous".

If you'd rather not take that on trust, the entire source code is public
and you can build it yourself:

    https://github.com/RokiTheWise/DClutter


WHAT IT DOES TO YOUR FILES
--------------------------

It only ever looks at your Downloads folder, plus any folders you
explicitly pick yourself.

  Keep      Does nothing at all. The file stays exactly where it is.
  Stage     Nothing is deleted straight away. Files are collected in a
            list, you review that list, and only then do they go to the
            Trash — where you can still get them back.
  Skip      Puts the file at the end of the queue to decide later.
  File      Moves the file into a folder you chose. Undo brings it back.

It never deletes anything permanently.


THE CONTROLS
------------

  Right arrow      Keep, next file
  Left arrow       Put in the trash pile, next file
  Space            Skip — it comes back at the end
  Up arrow         Choose a folder to file it into
  1, 2, 3          File it straight into folder 1, 2 or 3
  Return           Open the file so you can look at it properly
  Down arrow       Rename the current file
  Cmd + Z          Undo
  Shift + Cmd + Z   Redo (Cmd + Y also works)
  Cmd + Return     Review staged files and confirm moving them to Trash
  Cmd + N          Add a destination folder
  Cmd + ,          Open Settings
  ?                Show Controls & gestures in Settings

You can also swipe left and right on a trackpad, and swipe up with two
fingers to choose a folder.

The Stage, Skip, File, and Keep buttons below the preview work by click too.
Click a destination folder to file into it, or double-click the card to open
the file in its default app.

Hold Left or Right to move through files at a steady pace. The Settings
gear on the left lets you choose 0.5 to 8 files per second (3 by default).
At 0.5, each repeat waits two seconds. Releasing the key stops the hold.

Settings also has an optional Confirm Add folder switch, off by default.
Enable it to require Return or a click after a swipe highlights Add folder.

To sort a different folder, click the folder name at the top and pick one.
macOS will ask you to choose it yourself — an app like this can only reach
a folder you handed it. Each folder remembers its own progress, so you can
leave one half-sorted and come back to it.


SOMETHING WRONG?
----------------

It's a small project and I'm one person, so quite possibly. Please tell me
what happened:

    https://github.com/RokiTheWise/DClutter/issues


Any comments, suggestions, or feedback are highly appreciated — including
the small annoyances you'd normally not bother mentioning. Those are
usually the most useful ones.

Thank you for giving this a try.

    — DJ Enriquez :)
